title: Bugfix Run — Reproduce, Locate, Patch, Verify
description: A scoped defect worked end to end: a large model triages and plans, cheap models do the searching, and the patch loops through the test suite until it holds before a human is asked for anything.

nodes.name: Bug #4821
nodes.description: Session tokens survive logout on the mobile web client, so a shared device keeps the previous user signed in.
nodes.output:
Reported by: support triage rotation
Severity: S2 (security-adjacent)
Affected: web client >= 3.14.0, mobile Safari + Chrome Android

Steps:
  1. Sign in as user A on mobile web
  2. Tap Log out; confirm redirect to /login
  3. Navigate directly to /dashboard
  4. Observe: user A's dashboard renders, API calls succeed

Expected: redirect back to /login with a cleared session.

nodes.name: Triage & plan
nodes.description: Reads the report, decides this is a token-lifecycle bug rather than a routing bug, and splits the work into a cheap breadth pass and a focused depth pass.
nodes.prompt:
You are triaging bug #4821 in a React + Node monorepo.

Decide whether this is a routing/guard problem or a token-lifecycle problem, then produce a plan that spends as little of the expensive budget as possible: delegate breadth-first search to a small model and reserve deeper reasoning for the one or two files that actually matter.

Return: a hypothesis, a file-scope guess, and a task split.
nodes.output:
Hypothesis: logout clears the in-memory auth store but never revokes or clears the persisted refresh token, so the next bootstrap silently re-mints an access token.

Scope guess: src/auth/** plus whatever writes to localStorage.

Split:
  1. Haiku — map every read/write of the auth storage keys. Breadth only, no reasoning.
  2. Sonnet — reproduce against the real client so we are not fixing a phantom.
  3. Sonnet — trace the token lifecycle through the files Haiku surfaces.

nodes.name: Map auth surface
nodes.description: Breadth-first sweep for every site that touches the auth storage keys. No reasoning asked for — just an exhaustive list.
nodes.output:
5 files touch the auth storage keys:
  src/auth/tokenStore.ts     — read+write  gv.access, gv.refresh
  src/auth/useLogout.ts      — write       gv.access (clears)
  src/auth/bootstrap.ts      — read        gv.refresh
  src/api/client.ts          — read        gv.access
  src/auth/session.ts        — write       gv.refresh

Note: useLogout.ts clears gv.access but never touches gv.refresh.

nodes.name: Reproduce failure
nodes.description: Drives the real client to confirm the bug exists before anyone edits code, and captures the exact network sequence that re-mints the token.
nodes.output:
Reproduced on the first attempt.

Network trace after clicking Log out:
  POST /api/auth/logout          204
  GET  /dashboard                200   (should have redirected)
  POST /api/auth/refresh         200   <- re-mints an access token
  GET  /api/me                   200

localStorage after logout: gv.access removed, gv.refresh STILL PRESENT.
Confirms the orchestrator's hypothesis.

nodes.name: Trace token lifecycle
nodes.description: Reads only the five files the breadth pass surfaced and works out precisely which write is missing and why the guard never fires.
nodes.output:
Root cause, two independent defects:

1. useLogout.ts:31 calls tokenStore.clearAccess() where it must call tokenStore.clearAll().
   The refresh token is left in localStorage.

2. bootstrap.ts:22 treats the presence of a refresh token as sufficient to restore a session,
   without checking the server-side revocation list. So even a correct client-side clear would
   still be re-mintable from a stale token captured earlier.

Fixing only (1) closes the reported bug but leaves the weaker property. Recommend both.

nodes.name: Consolidate findings
nodes.description: Merges the repro trace and the lifecycle analysis into one patch brief, dropping the raw transcripts.
nodes.output:
Patch brief:
  - useLogout.ts:31   clearAccess() -> clearAll()
  - bootstrap.ts:22   verify refresh token against /api/auth/introspect before restoring
  - regression test: logout must leave zero gv.* keys in localStorage

nodes.name: Implement fix
nodes.description: Applies both fixes and adds the regression test. Took two passes — the first attempt broke a test that asserted the old, weaker behaviour.
nodes.logs:
attempt 1  patch applied, 3 specs failing
           session.spec.ts expected a surviving refresh token — that assertion encoded the bug
 attempt 2  updated session.spec.ts to assert full clearing, all specs green

nodes.name: bun test
nodes.description: Runs the auth suite plus the new regression spec.
nodes.output:
bun test v1.3.14

 src/auth/__tests__/logout.spec.ts       6 pass
 src/auth/__tests__/session.spec.ts     11 pass
 src/auth/__tests__/bootstrap.spec.ts    9 pass

 26 pass
 0 fail

nodes.name: Suite green?
nodes.description: Gates the human's attention: nobody is asked to review until the suite is clean.

nodes.name: Human review
nodes.description: The one human checkpoint in the run. Sees the patch brief and the diff, not the transcripts.
nodes.output: Approved by @onurseckin — asked for the introspect call to be behind the existing auth feature flag before merge; the agent applied it in the same PR.
